signal: Fiery launched a wave of AI tooling in 2026, including Fiery Scribe, an agentic AI that turns email job requests into ready-to-print jobs, plus JobFlow Pro and the FS700 Pro platform.

email.body1:
Barry, saw Fiery shipped a stack of AI tooling this year, including Fiery Scribe and JobFlow Pro on the new FS700 Pro platform.

For an SDR team, more product news means more inbound and accounts to touch than reps can follow up on, and response speed is where deals slip. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so your team covers more without new hires: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I had our AI SDR draft three personalized emails to Fiery's top three target accounts. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through them?
email.body2:
Barry, quick follow-up for Fiery.

Most SDR teams lose pipeline to slow follow-up and long ramp time on new reps, not lack of leads. Tightening that motion is usually the fastest lift you can show.

Worth 15 minutes? I will walk you through a teardown of your current outbound and three changes I would make. Our best practices alone tend to lift response rates 50 to 70 percent.
email.body3:
Barry, last bit of proof for Fiery.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how your reply rate likely compares to other print and software SDR teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Barry, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If speeding up follow-up without adding SDRs is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. A product wave keeps the team plenty busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your team's motion? I will tailor it to Fiery either way.
